origin: The user supplied Claude’s original mega list in this chat on October 25, 2026. The text below is preserved as the historical brief; current behavior follows STYLE.md and the later system-focused framing.

entries.originalBrief: a public list of the biggest unanswered questions in doing good, like Hilbert’s famous list of math problems. Fund people to solve them. This is your most memeable flagship.
entries.adaptation: All 23 problems are published and open for work. Prizes wait on the Question Bounties program.

entries.originalBrief: compares how different value systems rank causes (utilitarian, rights-based, justice, religious, community-first) and shows where they agree.
entries.adaptation: Live comparison and deliberation software uses eight draft framework sketches and 17 cause areas. Independent review by people who hold each view remains a milestone.

entries.originalBrief: compares the ways of giving itself, such as direct cash, policy advocacy, research funding, local mutual aid, volunteering, impact investing and prizes.
entries.adaptation: Live scenario and experiment-planning software is available. Its ranges are user assumptions, not empirical estimates; staffed comparative research and published findings remain milestones.

entries.originalBrief: maps every cause area by scale, neglect and solvability.
entries.adaptation: Live cause filters and evidence-capture software are available. Existing mappings are editorial hypotheses; a complete global funding or depth census has not been produced.

entries.originalBrief: systematic reviews of every major intervention.
entries.adaptation: Live protocol and study-extraction software links the draft Intervention Database. The workspace does not run literature searches or publish independently reviewed systematic reviews.

entries.originalBrief: re-runs famous charity impact studies to see if they hold up.
entries.adaptation: Live replication-planning software saves immutable local versions and exports protocols. Browser timestamps are not public registration; studies, participant safeguards and independent replications still need people and resources.

entries.originalBrief: on-the-ground audits that check charities do what they claim.
entries.adaptation: Live field-protocol planning software records methods, site visits by code, nonpersonal findings, limitations and correction plans. It does not conduct an audit, verify a charity or establish ethics approval or field partners.

entries.originalBrief: studies charities that failed or did harm, so others don’t repeat them.
entries.adaptation: Live case browsing and postmortem software are available. Archive entries remain drafts; cross-case findings and independent field investigations still need researchers and evidence.

entries.originalBrief: what actually worked across centuries, like smallpox eradication, the Green Revolution and Carnegie libraries.
entries.adaptation: Live filters, a source-linked timeline and a comparison notebook cover the current 13 draft cases. Broader historical coverage and independent source review remain open.

entries.originalBrief: people predict which interventions will work, and you score them over time.
entries.adaptation: Questions and forecasts are added by pull request and shown on the Forecasting Platform. Each forecast is scored when its question resolves.

entries.originalBrief: a standing team whose only job is attacking Charitology’s own recommendations.
entries.adaptation: Every entry page has a “Challenge a claim” link that opens a prefilled GitHub issue labeled red-team.

entries.originalBrief: one fund that always gives to the current best estimate of what’s best.
entries.adaptation: Live fund-planning software records proposals, conflicts, conditional allocations and a nonpayment authorization ledger, with internal and selected-field transparency exports. Legal authority, resources and independent governance remain unestablished; no money is accepted or moved.

entries.originalBrief: launches new charities to fill the gaps the research finds.
entries.adaptation: Live incubation software tracks a problem, existing-partner search, hypotheses, discovery, experiments, resources and launch gates. A functioning charity, funded cohort, mentors or legal home is not established.

entries.originalBrief: cash rewards for answering specific open questions.
entries.adaptation: Live bounty-design software links questions, answer criteria, conditional pledges, claim reviews and proposed decisions. It does not establish funding, an enforceable offer, independent judging or an awarded prize.

entries.originalBrief: an annual award for the best charity, research or idea.
entries.adaptation: Live nomination and jury-packet software records criteria, conflicts, reasons, dissent and review tasks. It produces no charity rating, selected winner or funded award.

entries.originalBrief: a credential for donors, nonprofit staff and advisors.
entries.adaptation: A printable nonaccredited course completion record is available from the shared ten-unit course progress. The proposed professional credential, independent exam and two-reviewer portfolio process do not operate.

entries.originalBrief: trains the next generation of researchers.
entries.adaptation: Live fellowship planning software includes a curriculum, project-code records, mentorship plans, milestones and readiness checks. No application is submitted, participant selected, stipend offered or credential granted.

entries.originalBrief: student clubs that spread the idea on campuses.
entries.adaptation: A local chapter-launch workspace includes six facilitated session agendas, responsibilities, tasks, draft constitution and invitation, handover prompts and JSON/CSV/Markdown exports. No recognized chapters or university partnerships are claimed.

entries.originalBrief: a free online course, the “Charity 101” of the field.
entries.adaptation: Ten-unit browser course with full textbook readings, twenty explained knowledge checks, saved practice notes and capstone, JSON backup and a printable nonaccredited completion record. No independent assessment is claimed.

entries.originalBrief: guidance for major donors and family foundations.
entries.adaptation: Live donor-deliberation software records goals, moral lenses, scenarios, questions, tradeoffs and follow-up actions. It does not appoint an adviser or provide personalized legal, tax or investment services.

entries.originalBrief: helps existing charities measure and improve their impact.
entries.adaptation: Live organization-improvement software records the system around a program, capacity, evaluation questions, change experiments and action plans. It does not establish a consulting engagement or independent evaluation.

entries.originalBrief: an annual conference.
entries.adaptation: Live summit-planning software includes a question-led program, sessions, responsibilities, access needs, costs and tentative UTC calendar export with overlap checks. No venue, speaker, invitation, registration or event is confirmed.

entries.originalBrief: applies the methods to local giving, like “the best charity in your city.”
entries.adaptation: A local research workspace records a geographic scope, sourced needs and activities, tentative depth descriptions and listening questions, then exports a methods-first brief. It is not a completed city census or a rating service.

entries.originalBrief: the best use of volunteer hours, not just dollars.
entries.adaptation: A working volunteer planner compares direct service, travel, preparation, skills and staff support, checks weekly capacity and logs actual hours and observations. Optional personal-cost arithmetic never estimates social value. An organization survey and placements are not operating.

entries.originalBrief: helps companies redesign workplace giving and matching.
entries.adaptation: A workplace matching calculator compares capped equal-gift scenarios, administration costs, budget shortfalls and participation sensitivity, alongside an editable policy and review checklist. It does not process gifts, payroll or establish company pilots.

entries.originalBrief: applies the research to government aid budgets.
entries.adaptation: A policy brief workspace compares a stated baseline and options, sourced claims, equity and participation, uncertainty and follow-up tasks. Optional discounted monetary scenarios show their assumptions without ranking options or claiming government adoption.

entries.originalBrief: a quiz on what you care about, which then shows your best-matched charities. This is how you make “all ways” personal.
entries.adaptation: Matches cause areas to your stated values. It does not recommend or rank named charities.

entries.originalBrief: spreads your giving across causes when you’re unsure which values are right.
entries.adaptation: Split a giving budget across causes when you aren’t sure which moral framework is right, compare two ways of doing it, and see how much they agree.

entries.originalBrief: search any charity and see its Charitology rating.
entries.adaptation: Searches the starter Charity Index and links to public registries. Depth labels are hypotheses, never ratings.

entries.originalBrief: on any donation page or GoFundMe, it shows the rating and higher-impact alternatives.
entries.adaptation: Live as a developer install for Chrome, Edge and Firefox. Store packages, listing copy and privacy documentation are prepared; store submission and approval are pending.

entries.originalBrief: shows “what $100 does here vs. there.”
entries.adaptation: Scenario estimates only where a published, dated intervention model exists. Different outcome units are not made interchangeable.

entries.originalBrief: puts any two charities side by side.
entries.adaptation: Compares interventions and their evidence, with no aggregate score or charity ranking.

entries.originalBrief: tracks your lifetime giving and its estimated impact.
entries.adaptation: Logs gifts, causes and self-described depth. It does not measure realized impact.

entries.originalBrief: a shareable year-end recap of your giving, Spotify Wrapped-style. Very memeable.
entries.adaptation: Turn a year of logged gifts into a card you can share, showing where your giving acted and the kind of giver it makes you, with or without the dollar amounts.

entries.originalBrief: give once and have it automatically divided across your portfolio.
entries.adaptation: The split planner is live. True one-click payment needs a licensed donation partner.

entries.originalBrief: builds charitable giving into a will or bequest.
entries.adaptation: A browser worksheet with sample language to discuss with a qualified adviser. It does not draft or execute a legal will.

entries.originalBrief: when a disaster hits, shows where money helps most, fast.
entries.adaptation: Sourced general guidance and a three-phase planner; no live disaster-specific charity recommendations.

entries.originalBrief: donate in someone’s name as a present.
entries.adaptation: Creates a printable or downloadable card. The actual donation happens through the charity.

entries.originalBrief: templates that help charities track their results.
entries.adaptation: Build a theory of change from the problem and its source to outcomes and indicators, with feedback from the people served, a comparison plan and a stop rule. Keep several drafts and export them as Markdown or JSON.

entries.originalBrief: open-source spreadsheets anyone can use and audit.
entries.adaptation: An open browser model with reproducible simulations and CSV export, rather than a hosted spreadsheet.

entries.originalBrief: a scoring framework for foundations reviewing proposals.
entries.adaptation: Review a proposal on nine dimensions, from source depth to risk of harm, keep unknowns as unknowns, compare your saved proposals side by side and export a review memo.

entries.originalBrief: a step-by-step vetting guide.
entries.adaptation: Check an organization against 25 questions on legitimacy, money, results, learning, its place in the system and red flags. Unknowns become questions to ask, and the report downloads as Markdown.

entries.originalBrief: a chat assistant that answers giving questions from your knowledge base.
entries.adaptation: Live as retrieval over the Record. The generative layer is designed and will cite the Record for every sentence.

entries.originalBrief: lets developers build your ratings into their apps and donation platforms.
entries.adaptation: Publishes the Record and data as static JSON. It has no charity ratings.

entries.originalBrief: the home for the forecasting tournaments.
entries.adaptation: Forecasts are proposed by public pull request; resolved questions are scored with Brier scores.

entries.originalBrief: the wiki of every cause, intervention and concept.
entries.adaptation: 26 searchable concept entries with source lists, review labels and downloadable reading dossiers. Entries remain editorial drafts pending contributor review.

entries.originalBrief: a database of charities worldwide with financials and ratings.
entries.adaptation: 16 transparent classification records with multi-filter browsing, registry links and research dossiers. Classifications remain draft hypotheses, not charity ratings.

entries.originalBrief: every intervention with its evidence strength and cost-effectiveness.
entries.adaptation: 15 sourced intervention records with six filters, side-by-side field comparison and research dossiers. Costs retain their original outcomes and caveats; review remains pending.

entries.originalBrief: a visual map of the world’s problems and how much funding each gets.
entries.adaptation: A working cause browser with linked intervention evidence. Worldwide funding is not estimated.

entries.originalBrief: where the world’s charity money goes compared with where the need is.
entries.adaptation: Financial baseline charts and a local depth census with classification coverage, undo and validated backups. No global depth estimate is claimed.

entries.originalBrief: the yearly “state of the world” for giving.
entries.adaptation: A complete Edition 0 baseline with financial definitions, project coverage, unknowns and a downloadable report.

entries.originalBrief: the top charities list.
entries.adaptation: A working nomination and method-review lab. No named-charity ranking is approved or published.

entries.originalBrief: which open problems got solved this year.
entries.adaptation: Where every open problem stands, whether open, partly answered or solved, updated as results come in.

entries.originalBrief: every relevant study, tagged and summarized.
entries.adaptation: An automatically assembled bibliography of cited sources, not every relevant study.

entries.originalBrief: post-mortems of charities and programs that didn’t work.
entries.adaptation: 8 searchable failure and mixed-result cases with lessons, sources and research dossiers. Inclusion does not estimate failure rates or judge the people involved.

entries.originalBrief: philanthropy’s greatest wins and losses.
entries.adaptation: 13 searchable cases with result, place and depth filters, full source lists and reading dossiers. This is a bounded draft collection, not a representative sample.

entries.originalBrief: where experts disagree and why. Publishing this openly builds trust.
entries.adaptation: 8 searchable disagreements with positions, cruxes, sources and discussion dossiers. The collection remains editorial and open to correction.

entries.originalBrief: needs and best options, country by country.
entries.adaptation: 217 country/economy data profiles and a local research desk. Locally coauthored narrative profiles remain a separate milestone.

entries.originalBrief: all cost-effectiveness estimates, uncertainty ranges included.
entries.adaptation: Every Charitology dataset as open JSON, plus the public datasets the field builds on.

entries.originalBrief: peer-reviewed research, which makes it a real academic field.
entries.adaptation: Real proposed-method papers and a manuscript desk. Independent peer review is not completed.

entries.originalBrief: the philosophy of giving across cultures and faiths, including Zakat, Tzedakah, Dāna and tithing.
entries.adaptation: 8 searchable traditions with practice, origin, lens, sources and reading dossiers. These draft sketches cannot represent a whole living tradition.

entries.originalBrief: the field’s founding textbook.
entries.adaptation: The complete ten-chapter textbook, full reading and print edition, download, search and private reading notebooks.

entries.originalBrief: a glossary of the field’s terms.
entries.adaptation: A searchable glossary with cross-references, definition study mode and CSV export.

entries.originalBrief: corrects misconceptions such as “low overhead means a good charity.”
entries.adaptation: 8 searchable belief analyses with verdict and condition filters, sources and discussion dossiers. Verdicts describe claims; contributor review remains pending.

entries.originalBrief: exactly how Charitology rates things, fully transparent.
entries.adaptation: A public handbook for evidence, depth, review and corrections. No charity rating method has been approved.

entries.originalBrief: the outward-facing voice.
entries.adaptation: Six actual MP3 episodes, transcripts and podcast RSS; a published letter and dedicated RSS. Email delivery is not configured.
